cards.note: Genesis 3:6 — *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.* *The first is the spirit of life, with which the constitution (of man) is created. The second is the sense of sight, with which ariseth desire.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 2:4) Reuben puts desire in the eye, and the oldest telling of it is in the garden, where the woman saw that the tree was pleasant to the eyes, and took. The Testament sorts the human frame into seven spirits and seven senses in a way Moses never does, so that arrangement is held loosely, but the road it describes, from seeing to wanting to taking, is the one Genesis had already walked.
cards.member_note: Genesis 3:6 — *it was pleasant to the eyes.* Desire came into the garden through the eye long before Reuben made his list.
cards.src_text: The first is the spirit of life, with which the constitution (of man) is created. The second is the sense of sight, with which ariseth desire.
cards.tgt_text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

cards.note: Job 31:1 — *I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?* *The first is the spirit of life, with which the constitution (of man) is created. The second is the sense of sight, with which ariseth desire.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 2:4) Job answers the same danger with a decision instead of a list of spirits: he made a covenant with his eyes before the question could even rise. Reuben, who is speaking out of his own repentance, is warning his sons in that same direction, toward guarding the gate of the eye.
cards.member_note: Job 31:1 — *I made a covenant with mine eyes.* The remedy for a wandering eye is a covenant, not a theory.
cards.src_text: The first is the spirit of life, with which the constitution (of man) is created. The second is the sense of sight, with which ariseth desire.
cards.tgt_text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

cards.note: Proverbs 7:22 — *He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;* *Wherefore it is the last in order of creation, and the first in that of youth, because it is filled with ignorance, and leadeth the youth as a blind man to a pit, and as a beast to a precipice.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 2:9) The Testament says desire leads the young man like a blind man to a pit and like a beast to a precipice. Proverbs paints the same road one street at a time, a young man following straight after her like an ox to the slaughter, and verse 23 adds that he goes on *and knoweth not that it is for his life*.
cards.member_note: Proverbs 7:22 — *as an ox goeth to the slaughter.* The young man is led away without seeing where the road ends.
cards.src_text: Wherefore it is the last in order of creation, and the first in that of youth, because it is filled with ignorance, and leadeth the youth as a blind man to a pit, and as a beast to a precipice.
cards.tgt_text: He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;

cards.note: Genesis 50:26 — *So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.* *And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 7:2) Reuben's sons lay him in a coffin and keep him there until they can carry him up from Egypt, just as Joseph was put in a coffin in Egypt after making the sons of Yashar'el (Israel) swear *ye shall carry up my bones from hence* (Genesis 50:25). The generation that died in Egypt died with its face toward the land.
cards.member_note: Genesis 50:26 — *he was put in a coffin in Egypt.* Joseph's coffin is the pattern the other sons followed.
cards.src_text: And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.
cards.tgt_text: So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 50:13 — *For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.* *And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 7:2) The Testament says Reuben was buried in Hebron in the cave where his father lay, and Genesis names that cave: the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought, where Jacob's sons buried their father. What the Testament adds about Reuben's own burial goes beyond what Genesis tells, and nothing here is built on it.
cards.member_note: Genesis 50:13 — *buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah.* The cave where Jacob lies is the one the Testament has in view.
cards.src_text: And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.
cards.tgt_text: For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

cards.note: Genesis 48:2 — *And one told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph cometh unto thee: and Yashar'el (Israel) strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.* *For when Simeon was sick, his sons came to visit him, and he strengthened himself and sat up and kissed them, and said:—* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 8:2) Simeon sits up on his sickbed and kisses his sons, and the picture is the one Genesis gives of Jacob when Joseph came to him: he strengthened himself and sat upon the bed. In both the dying man gathers what strength he has left so that his last words can be heard.
cards.member_note: Genesis 48:2 — *Yashar'el (Israel) strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.* A father rising from his sickbed to speak to his sons.
cards.src_text: For when Simeon was sick, his sons came to visit him, and he strengthened himself and sat up and kissed them, and said:—
cards.tgt_text: And one told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph cometh unto thee: and Yashar'el (Israel) strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.

cards.note: Genesis 50:26 — *So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.* *The copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spake to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, at which time Joseph, his brother, died.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 8:1) The Testament dates Simeon's last words to the year Joseph died, and Genesis closes Joseph's life with the same death and the coffin in Egypt. Simeon, who once hated Joseph, speaks his farewell in the year the brother he wronged is laid to rest.
cards.member_note: Genesis 50:26 — *So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old.* The Testament dates Simeon's last words by this death.
cards.src_text: The copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spake to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, at which time Joseph, his brother, died.
cards.tgt_text: So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

cards.note: Psalm 77:20 — *Thou leddest thy people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.* *And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 16:2) Simeon's sons stay in Egypt until the day of their departure *by the hand of Moses*, and the psalm uses almost the same words when it remembers the exodus as a flock led out by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
cards.member_note: Psalm 77:20 — *by the hand of Moses and Aaron.* The exodus remembered as a flock led out by Moses.
cards.src_text: And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.
cards.tgt_text: Thou leddest thy people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

cards.note: Exodus 12:41 — *And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Yahuah (LORD) went out from the land of Egypt.* *And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 16:2) The day of departure is the day Exodus fixes, at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, *the selfsame day* that all the hosts of Yahuah (the LORD) went out of Egypt. Simeon's sons are the generations waiting for that day.
cards.member_note: Exodus 12:41 — *all the hosts of Yahuah (LORD) went out from the land of Egypt.* The day the waiting in Egypt ended.
cards.src_text: And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Yahuah (LORD) went out from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 49:1 — *And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.* *The copy of the words of Levi, the things which he ordained unto his sons, according to all that they should do, and what things should befall them until the day of judgment.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 17:1) Levi gathers his sons to ordain what they are to do and what will befall them until the day of judgment, in the pattern of Jacob, who called his sons together to tell them what would befall them in the last days. A father's last word is a word about what is coming.
cards.member_note: Genesis 49:1 — *that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.* Jacob called his sons together to say what would befall them.
cards.src_text: The copy of the words of Levi, the things which he ordained unto his sons, according to all that they should do, and what things should befall them until the day of judgment.
cards.tgt_text: And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.

cards.note: 2 Peter 1:14 — *Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) hath shewed me.* *He was sound in health when he called them to him; for it had been revealed to him that he should die. And when they were gathered together he said to them:* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 17:2) Levi was sound in health when he called his sons, because it had been revealed to him that he should die. Peter says the same of himself: he knew that shortly he must put off his tabernacle, as it had been shewed him, and so he spoke while he could.
cards.member_note: 2 Peter 1:14 — *shortly I must put off this my tabernacle.* One who knew the hour was near and spoke while he could.
cards.src_text: He was sound in health when he called them to him; for it had been revealed to him that he should die. And when they were gathered together he said to them:
cards.tgt_text: Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) hath shewed me.

cards.note: Genesis 34:7 — *And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.* *Because also they had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) by defiling my sister. And we departed and came to Bethel.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 23:3) Levi calls the defiling of his sister *folly in Yashar'el (Israel)*, and that is Genesis's own phrase, spoken when the sons of Jacob came in from the field and heard what had been done. The words name the wrong done to Dinah as a wrong done to the whole house.
cards.member_note: Genesis 34:7 — *he had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel).* The same words the brothers used when they heard.
cards.src_text: Because also they had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) by defiling my sister. And we departed and came to Bethel.
cards.tgt_text: And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.

cards.note: Genesis 34:30 — *And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.* *For from this day forward shall Shechem be called a city of imbeciles; for as a man mocketh a fool, so did we mock them,* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 23:2) Levi tells how they mocked the Shechemites, and leaves it there. Genesis keeps Jacob's answer: he told Simeon and Levi they had troubled him and put his whole house in danger, and at the end of his life he said *Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce* (Genesis 49:7). The two voices stand side by side in scripture and the reader is allowed to hear both.
cards.member_note: Genesis 34:30 — *Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land.* Jacob's answer to the brothers' deed, kept in scripture beside Levi's account.
cards.src_text: For from this day forward shall Shechem be called a city of imbeciles; for as a man mocketh a fool, so did we mock them,
cards.tgt_text: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.

cards.note: Genesis 35:12 — *And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.* *And I said to my father Jacob: By thee will Yahuah (Lord) destroy the Canaanites, and will give their land to thee and to thy seed after thee.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 23:1) Levi tells his father that Yahuah (the Lord) will give the land to him and to his seed after him, and that is the promise Elohim (God) renewed to Jacob at Beth-el: the land given to Abraham and Isaac, to thee and to thy seed after thee. Levi is speaking as one standing in the line of the promise.
cards.member_note: Genesis 35:12 — *to thy seed after thee will I give the land.* The promise Levi tells his father he is trusting.
cards.src_text: And I said to my father Jacob: By thee will Yahuah (Lord) destroy the Canaanites, and will give their land to thee and to thy seed after thee.
cards.tgt_text: And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.

cards.note: Numbers 26:59 — *And the name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, whom her mother bare to Levi in Egypt: and she bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.* *And Jochebed was born in Egypt, in my sixty-fourth year, for I was renowned then in the midst of my brethren.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 27:8) Levi says Jochebed was born in Egypt in his sixty-fourth year, and Numbers records the same birth in its own words: she was the daughter of Levi, whom her mother bare to Levi in Egypt, and she bare Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The Testament supplies the year that Numbers leaves unsaid.
cards.member_note: Numbers 26:59 — *whom her mother bare to Levi in Egypt.* The birth of the woman who would be the mother of Moses and Aaron.
cards.src_text: And Jochebed was born in Egypt, in my sixty-fourth year, for I was renowned then in the midst of my brethren.
cards.tgt_text: And the name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, whom her mother bare to Levi in Egypt: and she bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.

cards.note: Exodus 2:22 — *And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.* *And she conceived and bare a son, and I called his name Gersam, for we were sojourners in our land.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 27:2) Levi gives Gersam his name because they were sojourners, and scripture gives that same reason for the same kind of name when Moses names his own son in Midian. The name Gersam, which the lists of the sons of Levi spell Gershon, is the name of a stranger in a strange land.
cards.member_note: Exodus 2:22 — *I have been a stranger in a strange land.* The reason given for naming a son from the house of Levi.
cards.src_text: And she conceived and bare a son, and I called his name Gersam, for we were sojourners in our land.
cards.tgt_text: And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.

cards.note: Numbers 3:31 — *And their charge shall be the ark, and the table, and the candlestick, and the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary wherewith they minister, and the hanging, and all the service thereof.* *And I saw in a vision that he was standing on high in the midst of all the congregation.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 27:5) Levi sees in a vision Kohath standing on high in the midst of the congregation, and Numbers gives that standing its shape: the charge of the sons of Kohath was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. The vision and the charge fit together.
cards.member_note: Numbers 3:31 — *their charge shall be the ark, and the table, and the candlestick.* What Kohath's house was lifted up to carry.
cards.src_text: And I saw in a vision that he was standing on high in the midst of all the congregation.
cards.tgt_text: And their charge shall be the ark, and the table, and the candlestick, and the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary wherewith they minister, and the hanging, and all the service thereof.

cards.note: Exodus 6:18 — *And the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath were an hundred thirty and three years.* *And the sons of Kohath, Ambram, Issachar, Hebron, and Ozeel.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 28:2) Levi lists the four sons of Kohath as Ambram, Issachar, Hebron, and Ozeel, and Exodus lists the same four by the spellings that stand in the canon: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. The names are spelled a little differently but the family is the same.
cards.member_note: Exodus 6:18 — *the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel.* The same four sons of Kohath in the canon's spelling.
cards.src_text: And the sons of Kohath, Ambram, Issachar, Hebron, and Ozeel.
cards.tgt_text: And the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath were an hundred thirty and three years.

cards.note: Exodus 6:20 — *And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were an hundred and thirty and seven years.* *And in my ninety-fourth year Ambram took Jochebed my daughter to him to wife, for they were born in one day, he and my daughter.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 28:4) Ambram takes Jochebed, Levi's daughter, to wife, and Exodus says that Amram took Jochebed and she bare him Aaron and Moses. The marriage that brought Moses and Aaron into the world was a marriage inside the house of Levi.
cards.member_note: Exodus 6:20 — *And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses.* The marriage inside Levi's house that gave Yashar'el (Israel) Aaron and Moses.
cards.src_text: And in my ninety-fourth year Ambram took Jochebed my daughter to him to wife, for they were born in one day, he and my daughter.
cards.tgt_text: And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were an hundred and thirty and seven years.

cards.note: Genesis 15:16 — *But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.* *And behold, my children, ye are a third generation.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 28:6) Levi tells his sons *ye are a third generation*, and a man who keeps his years and the births of his sons this carefully is a man counting down a promise. Genesis had said that in the fourth generation they would come back, because the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full.
cards.member_note: Genesis 15:16 — *in the fourth generation they shall come hither again.* The promise that Levi's careful counting is waiting on.
cards.src_text: And behold, my children, ye are a third generation.
cards.tgt_text: But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.

cards.note: Ezekiel 5:11 — *Wherefore, as I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity.* *Therefore the temple, which Yahuah (Lord) shall choose, shall be laid waste through your uncleanness, and ye shall be captives throughout all nations.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 31:1) Levi says the temple will be laid waste through the uncleanness of the sons, and Ezekiel gives Yahuah's (the Lord's) own reason for the same ruin: the sanctuary had been defiled with detestable things. The cause named is the defiling, never the temple and never the law that taught them what was clean.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 5:11 — *thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things.* The cause of the laying waste.
cards.src_text: Therefore the temple, which Yahuah (Lord) shall choose, shall be laid waste through your uncleanness, and ye shall be captives throughout all nations.
cards.tgt_text: Wherefore, as I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 28:37 — *And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither Yahuah (LORD) shall lead thee.* *And ye shall be an abomination unto them, and ye shall receive reproach and everlasting shame from the righteous judgment of Elohim (God).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 31:2) Levi's word that they will be an abomination among the nations is the warning Moses set down in the curses, that the scattering would make them an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword. That curse is the judgment that follows turning away from the commandments, not the commandments themselves.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 28:37 — *an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations.* The shame of the scattering, foretold.
cards.src_text: And ye shall be an abomination unto them, and ye shall receive reproach and everlasting shame from the righteous judgment of Elohim (God).
cards.tgt_text: And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither Yahuah (LORD) shall lead thee.

cards.note: Leviticus 26:42 — *Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.* *And if you were not to receive mercy through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers, not one of our seed should be left upon the earth.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 31:4) Levi's reason for the mercy, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers, is the reason Yahuah (the LORD) gave in the Torah long before the scattering: even in the land of their enemies he would remember his covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, and the land.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 26:42 — *Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac.* The fathers' covenant remembered in exile.
cards.src_text: And if you were not to receive mercy through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers, not one of our seed should be left upon the earth.
cards.tgt_text: Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.

cards.note: Isaiah 1:9 — *Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.* *And if you were not to receive mercy through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers, not one of our seed should be left upon the earth.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 31:4) Levi says that without mercy for the fathers' sake not one of the seed would be left upon the earth, and Isaiah says it as a remnant: except Yahuah Tseva'ot (the LORD of hosts) had left a very small remnant, they would have been as Sodom.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 1:9 — *Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant.* Only mercy leaves a remnant.
cards.src_text: And if you were not to receive mercy through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers, not one of our seed should be left upon the earth.
cards.tgt_text: Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

cards.note: Daniel 9:24 — *Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.* *And whereas ye have heard concerning the seventy weeks, hear also concerning the priesthood.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:1) Levi speaks of the seventy weeks and goes straight on to the priesthood, as Daniel's seventy weeks are set upon his people and his holy city and end with the anointing of the most Holy. The Testament lays its own scheme of jubilees and priests over the weeks, and Daniel's verse is read here only as Daniel.
cards.member_note: Daniel 9:24 — *Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city.* The seventy weeks Levi has in mind.
cards.src_text: And whereas ye have heard concerning the seventy weeks, hear also concerning the priesthood.
cards.tgt_text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.

cards.note: Malachi 2:6 — *The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.* *For in each jubilee there shall be a priesthood. And in the first jubilee, the first who is anointed to the priesthood shall be great, and shall speak to Elohim (God) as to a father. And his priesthood shall be perfect with Yahuah (Lord), [and in the day of his gladness shall he arise for the salvation of the world].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:2) Of the first priest Levi says he speaks to Elohim (God) as to a father and that his priesthood is perfect with Yahuah (the Lord). Malachi describes the true priest in the same way, one in whose mouth was the law of truth, who walked with Yahuah in peace and equity. The bracketed words at the end of Levi's verse are set off in the text as an addition, and this note rests only on what comes before them.
cards.member_note: Malachi 2:6 — *The law of truth was in his mouth.* The priest as Malachi remembers him.
cards.src_text: For in each jubilee there shall be a priesthood. And in the first jubilee, the first who is anointed to the priesthood shall be great, and shall speak to Elohim (God) as to a father. And his priesthood shall be perfect with Yahuah (Lord), [and in the day of his gladness shall he arise for the salvation of the world].
cards.tgt_text: The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.

cards.note: Ezra 1:5 — *Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit Elohim (God) had raised, to go up to build the house of Yahuah (LORD) which is in Jerusalem.* *And in the fifth week they shall return to their desolate country, and shall renew the house of Yahuah (Lord).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:10) The return in the fifth week to the desolate country, to renew the house of Yahuah (the Lord), is the return Ezra records, when the chief of the fathers of Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin, with the priests and Levites, rose up to build the house in Jerusalem.
cards.member_note: Ezra 1:5 — *to go up to build the house of Yahuah (LORD) which is in Jerusalem.* The return that renewed the house.
cards.src_text: And in the fifth week they shall return to their desolate country, and shall renew the house of Yahuah (Lord).

cards.note: Malachi 2:8 — *But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* *And in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless, lascivious, abusers of children and beasts.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:11) Levi's seventh week brings priests who are idolaters, lovers of money, and lawless. cards.member_note: Jubilees 38:12 — *they paid tribute to Jacob and to his sons always.* Peace made, and tribute paid.
cards.src_text: Then they asked from us terms of peace; and having taken counsel with our father, we received them as tributaries.

cards.note: Genesis 30:18 — *And Leah said, Elohim (God) hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.* *And Jacob knew Leah, and she 'conceived and' bare me, and on account of the hire I was called Issachar.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 62:15) Genesis gives the reason for the name in Leah's own mouth, and the Testament of Issachar has the son say the same thing back: "on account of the hire I was called Issachar." The name is a receipt for the night Leah paid for.
cards.member_note: Genesis 30:18 — *Elohim (God) hath given me my hire … and she called his name Issachar.* The name Issachar is tied to the hire Leah paid, and the Testament of Issachar says the same.
cards.src_text: And Jacob knew Leah, and she 'conceived and' bare me, and on account of the hire I was called Issachar.
cards.tgt_text: And Leah said, Elohim (God) hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.

cards.note: Genesis 30:14 — *And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son’s mandrakes.* *For Reuben 'my brother' brought in mandrakes from the field, and Rachel met him and took them.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 62:3) Genesis puts Reuben in the field in the days of wheat harvest and has Rachel ask Leah for the mandrakes, while the Testament of Issachar has Rachel meet him and take them. The two tellings agree on where the quarrel between the sisters began.
cards.member_note: Genesis 30:14 — *Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son’s mandrakes.* Reuben brings the mandrakes home and the sisters' quarrel begins, in Genesis as in the Testament of Issachar.
cards.src_text: For Reuben 'my brother' brought in mandrakes from the field, and Rachel met him and took them.
cards.tgt_text: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son’s mandrakes.

cards.note: Genesis 30:16 — *And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for surely I have hired thee with my son’s mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.* *Nevertheless, for the mandrakes I am hiring Jacob to thee for one night.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 62:14) Both tellings call the night a purchase: Genesis has Leah say she had hired Jacob with her son's mandrakes, and the Testament of Issachar has Rachel say "I am hiring Jacob to thee for one night." The Testament only changes who is speaking.
cards.member_note: Genesis 30:16 — *I have hired thee with my son’s mandrakes.* Jacob's night with Leah is bargained for with mandrakes, just as the Testament of Issachar says.
cards.src_text: Nevertheless, for the mandrakes I am hiring Jacob to thee for one night.
cards.tgt_text: And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for surely I have hired thee with my son’s mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.

cards.note: Genesis 29:25 — *And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?* *For thou art not his wife, but in craft wert taken to him in my stead.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 62:12) Rachel's complaint in the Testament of Issachar, that Leah was taken to Jacob "in craft," is the very thing Jacob says to Laban the morning after: "wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?" Laban's trick lies underneath the whole quarrel over the mandrakes.
cards.member_note: Genesis 29:25 — *wherefore then hast thou beguiled me.* Laban's deception, the root of the sisters' rivalry, is what the Testament of Issachar calls craft.
cards.src_text: For thou art not his wife, but in craft wert taken to him in my stead.
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?

cards.note: Genesis 30:22 — *And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.* *For on the morrow also she again gave up Jacob. Because of the mandrakes, therefore, Yahuah (Lord) hearkened to Rachel.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 63:4) Genesis says Elohim (God) remembered Rachel and hearkened to her, and the Testament of Issachar says the very same of Yahuah (the Lord): He hearkened to Rachel. The mandrakes are not the point; the hearing is.
cards.member_note: Genesis 30:22 — *And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.* Rachel is heard and her womb is opened, in Genesis and in the Testament of Issachar.
cards.src_text: For on the morrow also she again gave up Jacob. Because of the mandrakes, therefore, Yahuah (Lord) hearkened to Rachel.
cards.tgt_text: And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

cards.note: Genesis 30:23 — *And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, Elohim (God) hath taken away my reproach:* *For He knew that for the sake of children she wished to company with Jacob, and not for lust of pleasure.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 63:3) The Testament of Issachar says Rachel wished for children and "not for lust of pleasure," and Genesis shows what she was really carrying: the reproach of barrenness, which Elohim (God) took away when Joseph was born.
cards.member_note: Genesis 30:23 — *Elohim (God) hath taken away my reproach.* What Rachel longed for was a son and an end to her reproach, as the Testament of Issachar says.
cards.src_text: For He knew that for the sake of children she wished to company with Jacob, and not for lust of pleasure.
cards.tgt_text: And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, Elohim (God) hath taken away my reproach:

cards.note: Genesis 30:24 — *And she called his name Joseph; and said, Yahuah (LORD) shall add to me another son.* *Then appeared to Jacob an angel of Yahuah (Lord), saying: Two children shall Rachel bear, inasmuch as she hath refused company with her husband, and hath chosen continency.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 63:1) When the Testament of Issachar has an angel tell Jacob that Rachel shall bear "Two children," it is looking at the same hope Rachel voices at Joseph's birth, a second son to follow the first. Genesis does not mention the angel, so the reader should set the angel's word beside Rachel's and let Genesis stand as the record.
cards.member_note: Genesis 30:24 — *Yahuah (LORD) shall add to me another son.* Rachel asks Yahuah (the LORD) for one more son, which the Testament of Issachar reads as two children in all.
cards.src_text: Then appeared to Jacob an angel of Yahuah (Lord), saying: Two children shall Rachel bear, inasmuch as she hath refused company with her husband, and hath chosen continency.
cards.tgt_text: And she called his name Joseph; and said, Yahuah (LORD) shall add to me another son.

cards.note: Genesis 14:18 — *And Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the El Elyon (most high God).* *For though she desired them, she eat them not, but offered them in the house of Yahuah (Lord), presenting them to the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) who was at that time.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 63:5) The Testament of Issachar says Rachel offered the mandrakes in the house of Yahuah (the Lord) to the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) of that time. Genesis does tell of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) as priest of the El Elyon (most high God) in the days of Abraham, but nowhere says that mandrakes were brought to any priest, so the reader has Genesis for the priest and the Testament for the offering and no more than that.
cards.member_note: Genesis 14:18 — *priest of the El Elyon (most high God).* Genesis names a priest of the El Elyon (most high God) in the patriarchs' own time; the mandrake offering is the Testament's alone.
cards.src_text: For though she desired them, she eat them not, but offered them in the house of Yahuah (Lord), presenting them to the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) who was at that time.
cards.tgt_text: And Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the El Elyon (most high God).

cards.note: Proverbs 14:29 — *He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.* *For anger is an evil thing, my children, for it troubleth even the soul itself.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 81:1) The Testament of Dan says anger "troubleth even the soul itself," and Proverbs says the same from the other side: the man quick to wrath is the one who lifts folly high. Both begin with what anger does to the man who carries it.
cards.member_note: Proverbs 14:29 — *he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.* Quickness to wrath is folly, as the Testament of Dan says of the angry soul.
cards.src_text: For anger is an evil thing, my children, for it troubleth even the soul itself.
cards.tgt_text: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

cards.note: James 1:20 — *For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of Elohim (God).* *And when the body does all these things, the soul justifieth what is done, since it seeth not aright.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 81:3) The Testament of Dan says the soul of an angry man "justifieth what is done, since it seeth not aright." James answers that wrath cannot produce the righteousness Elohim (God) asks for, however right it feels to the one who is angry.
cards.member_note: James 1:20 — *the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of Elohim (God).* Anger persuades the angry man that he is right, but it never makes him so.
cards.src_text: And when the body does all these things, the soul justifieth what is done, since it seeth not aright.
cards.tgt_text: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Proverbs 29:22 — *An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.* *And though the wrathful man be weak, yet hath he a power twofold of that which is by nature; for wrath ever aideth such in lawlessness.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 81:5) The Testament of Dan says wrath "ever aideth such in lawlessness," and Proverbs says that a furious man aboundeth in transgression. The two lines are one observation: anger multiplies sin.
cards.member_note: Proverbs 29:22 — *a furious man aboundeth in transgression.* Anger feeds on itself and abounds in transgression, as the Testament of Dan teaches.
cards.src_text: And though the wrathful man be weak, yet hath he a power twofold of that which is by nature; for wrath ever aideth such in lawlessness.
cards.tgt_text: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.

cards.note: Ephesians 4:27 — *Neither give place to the devil.* *This spirit goeth always with lying 'at the right hand of Satan, that with cruelty and lying' his works may be wrought.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 81:6) The Testament of Dan joins anger to lying and puts both at the right hand of Satan. The short line in Ephesians gives the same warning in a few words, that anger can open a door.
cards.member_note: Ephesians 4:27 — *Neither give place to the devil.* Anger is a door that must not be left open, a warning the Testament of Dan also gives.
cards.src_text: This spirit goeth always with lying 'at the right hand of Satan, that with cruelty and lying' his works may be wrought.
cards.tgt_text: Neither give place to the devil.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:18 — *Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten Elohim (God) that formed thee.* *[Nevertheless, 'Dan' prophesied unto them that they should forget their Elohim (God), and should be alienated from the land of their inheritance 'and from the race of Israel', and from the family of 'their seed'.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 85:3) The Testament of Dan says his sons "should forget their Elohim (God)," and Moses had already put that charge in a song: Yashar'el (Israel) forgot Elohim (God) who formed them. The bracketed sentence is Dan's sorrow, and the song is Moses' warning.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 32:18 — *hast forgotten Elohim (God) that formed thee.* Forgetting Elohim (God) is the old charge in Moses' song, and the Testament of Dan repeats it over his own tribe.
cards.src_text: [Nevertheless, 'Dan' prophesied unto them that they should forget their Elohim (God), and should be alienated from the land of their inheritance 'and from the race of Israel', and from the family of 'their seed'.]
cards.tgt_text: Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten Elohim (God) that formed thee.

cards.note: Judges 18:30 — *And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.* *[Nevertheless, 'Dan' prophesied unto them that they should forget their Elohim (God), and should be alienated from the land of their inheritance 'and from the race of Israel', and from the family of 'their seed'.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 85:3) Scripture records how the tribe of Dan set up a graven image for itself and kept priests for it until the day of the captivity of the land. This is the scripture beside the Testament of Dan's saying that his sons would be "alienated from the land of their inheritance." The sentence in the Testament is bracketed in the translation, so the reader should let Judges stand as the witness.
cards.member_note: Judges 18:30 — *the children of Dan set up the graven image.* Dan's turning aside to an image is told in Judges and lies behind the Testament of Dan's foretelling.
cards.src_text: [Nevertheless, 'Dan' prophesied unto them that they should forget their Elohim (God), and should be alienated from the land of their inheritance 'and from the race of Israel', and from the family of 'their seed'.]
cards.tgt_text: And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

cards.note: Genesis 49:31 — *There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.* *And his sons buried him. And after that they carried up 'his bones', and placed them near Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 85:2) The Testament of Dan says his sons carried up his bones and "placed them near Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob." Genesis names the cave where Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah were buried, which is the burying place the fathers' sons were laid beside. It does not say where Dan was buried, so the Testament speaks for itself there.
cards.member_note: Genesis 49:31 — *There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife.* Genesis names the patriarchs' burying place, beside which the Testament of Dan says Dan was laid.
cards.src_text: And his sons buried him. And after that they carried up 'his bones', and placed them near Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob.
cards.tgt_text: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.

cards.note: Genesis 45:28 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) said, It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.* *Then my father saith unto me: I believe Elohim (God) that Joseph liveth, for I see 'always' that Yahuah (Lord) numbereth him with you.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 92:2) In the Testament of Naphtali, Jacob says he believes Elohim (God) that Joseph lives, and when the news finally comes in Genesis the old man says it plainly: "Joseph my son is yet alive." What he held in hope the wagons made certain.
cards.member_note: Genesis 45:28 — *Joseph my son is yet alive.* Jacob's faith that Joseph lives, in the Testament of Naphtali, becomes his plain word in Genesis.
cards.src_text: Then my father saith unto me: I believe Elohim (God) that Joseph liveth, for I see 'always' that Yahuah (Lord) numbereth him with you.
cards.tgt_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) said, It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.

cards.note: Genesis 37:11 — *And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.* *These two dreams I told to my father; and he said to me: These things must be fulfilled in their season, after that Yashar'el (Israel) hath endured many things.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 92:1) Joseph's father in Genesis "observed the saying" of the dreams, and in the Testament of Naphtali he tells his son the dreams must be fulfilled in their season, after Yashar'el (Israel) has endured many things. Both show a father who kept the dreams in mind.
cards.member_note: Genesis 37:11 — *And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.* Jacob did not forget Joseph's dreams, as Genesis and the Testament of Naphtali both show.
cards.src_text: These two dreams I told to my father; and he said to me: These things must be fulfilled in their season, after that Yashar'el (Israel) hath endured many things.
cards.tgt_text: And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.

cards.note: Genesis 37:35 — *And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.* *And he said, weeping: Ah me, my son, Joseph, thou livest, though I behold thee not, and thou seest not Jacob that begat thee.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 92:3) Genesis tells that Jacob refused comfort and said he would go down mourning to the grave, and the Testament of Naphtali has him weeping, "Ah me, my son, Joseph, thou livest, though I behold thee not." The tears are the same; the Testament adds that his hope was alive under them.
cards.member_note: Genesis 37:35 — *but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning.* Jacob's mourning for Joseph, the weeping in the Testament of Naphtali, is the same grief Genesis records.
cards.src_text: And he said, weeping: Ah me, my son, Joseph, thou livest, though I behold thee not, and thou seest not Jacob that begat thee.
cards.tgt_text: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.

cards.note: Genesis 37:33 — *And he knew it, and said, It is my son’s coat; an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces.* *He caused me also, therefore, to weep by these words, and I burned in my heart to declare that 'Joseph' had been sold, but I feared my brethren.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 92:4) Naphtali confesses he burned to declare that Joseph had been sold, but feared his brethren. Genesis shows what the silence cost, for Jacob looked at the coat and cried that Joseph was without doubt rent in pieces.
cards.member_note: Genesis 37:33 — *an evil beast hath devoured him.* The brothers' silence let Jacob believe a lie, and the Testament of Naphtali says one of them longed to speak.
cards.src_text: He caused me also, therefore, to weep by these words, and I burned in my heart to declare that 'Joseph' had been sold, but I feared my brethren.
cards.tgt_text: And he knew it, and said, It is my son’s coat; an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces.

cards.note: Genesis 49:29 — *And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,* *And when he had charged them with many such words, he exhorted them that they should remove his bones to Hebron, and that they should bury him with his fathers.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 94:1) Naphtali charges his sons to bury him with his fathers, as Jacob had charged his own. The Testament of Naphtali and Genesis speak with one voice at the deathbed: a patriarch who wishes to lie with his people.
cards.member_note: Genesis 49:29 — *bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite* A dying patriarch asks to be buried with his fathers, as Jacob did in Genesis and Naphtali does in his Testament.
cards.src_text: And when he had charged them with many such words, he exhorted them that they should remove his bones to Hebron, and that they should bury him with his fathers.
cards.tgt_text: And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

cards.note: Genesis 23:19 — *And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.* *And when he had charged them with many such words, he exhorted them that they should remove his bones to Hebron, and that they should bury him with his fathers.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 94:1) The Testament of Naphtali names Hebron as the place for his bones, and Genesis is where Hebron first becomes a burying place, when Abraham buried Sarah there. The fathers' graves are the reason Naphtali asks to be taken there.
cards.member_note: Genesis 23:19 — *the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.* Abraham buried Sarah at Hebron, the cave to which Naphtali asks to be carried.
cards.src_text: And when he had charged them with many such words, he exhorted them that they should remove his bones to Hebron, and that they should bury him with his fathers.
cards.tgt_text: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 49:33 — *And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.* *And when he had eaten and drunken with a merry heart, he covered his face and died.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 94:2) The Testament of Naphtali says he "covered his face and died," and Genesis closes Jacob's life with the same plainness: he gathered up his feet and was gathered to his people. In both, a father finishes his commands and then departs.
cards.member_note: Genesis 49:33 — *and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.* Naphtali ends his charge and dies like Jacob, gathered to his people.
cards.src_text: And when he had eaten and drunken with a merry heart, he covered his face and died.
cards.tgt_text: And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.

cards.note: Genesis 50:12 — *And his sons did unto him according as he commanded them:* *And his sons did according to all that Naphtali their father had commanded them.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 94:3) The Testament of Naphtali says his sons "did according to all that Naphtali their father had commanded them." Genesis has the very same obedience from Jacob's sons when they buried their father.
cards.member_note: Genesis 50:12 — *his sons did unto him according as he commanded them.* Sons who carry out a dying father's command are the picture in both Genesis and the Testament of Naphtali.
cards.src_text: And his sons did according to all that Naphtali their father had commanded them.
cards.tgt_text: And his sons did unto him according as he commanded them:

cards.note: Genesis 25:8 — *Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.* *And when he had said these things unto them, he commanded saying: Bury me in Hebron. And he fell asleep and died at a good old age.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 110:1) Asher falls asleep "at a good old age," the same words Genesis uses of Abraham. Both end full of days and gathered to their people.
cards.member_note: Genesis 25:8 — *died in a good old age.* Asher's end in the Testament of Asher is told in the words used of Abraham.
cards.src_text: And when he had said these things unto them, he commanded saying: Bury me in Hebron. And he fell asleep and died at a good old age.
cards.tgt_text: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.

cards.note: Genesis 49:31 — *There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.* *And when he had said these things unto them, he commanded saying: Bury me in Hebron. And he fell asleep and died at a good old age.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 110:1) Asher's command, "Bury me in Hebron," asks for the place where Genesis says Abraham and Sarah lay, and Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah. The fathers' burying place is what his request is aimed at.
cards.member_note: Genesis 49:31 — *There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife.* Hebron holds the fathers' graves, which is why Asher asks to be carried there.
cards.src_text: And when he had said these things unto them, he commanded saying: Bury me in Hebron. And he fell asleep and died at a good old age.
cards.tgt_text: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.

cards.note: Genesis 50:13 — *For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.* *And his sons did as he had commanded them, and they carried him up to Hebron, and buried him with his fathers.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 110:2) The sons of Asher "carried him up to Hebron, and buried him with his fathers," and Genesis tells how Jacob's sons carried their father to the same cave of Machpelah. The Testament of Asher closes with the same obedience.
cards.member_note: Genesis 50:13 — *his sons carried him into the land of Canaan.* Jacob's sons carried him to Machpelah just as Asher's sons carry him to Hebron.
cards.src_text: And his sons did as he had commanded them, and they carried him up to Hebron, and buried him with his fathers.

cards.note: Genesis 39:9 — *There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim (God)?* *I therefore, when I heard this, rent my garments, and said unto her: Woman, reverence Elohim (God), and do not this evil deed, lest thou be destroyed; for know indeed that I will declare this thy device unto all men.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 115:2) Joseph in the Testament of Joseph tells the woman to "reverence Elohim (God)" and refuse this evil deed, and in Genesis his refusal turns on the same fear: how can he do this great wickedness and sin against Elohim (God)? The sin is first against Elohim (God), and only then against the master.
cards.member_note: Genesis 39:9 — *how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim (God).* Joseph refuses on account of Elohim (God), in Genesis and in the Testament of Joseph alike.

cards.note: Exodus 20:14 — *Thou shalt not commit adultery.* *'And' again, at another time she said unto me: If thou wilt not commit adultery, I will kill my husband by poison, and take thee to be my husband.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 115:1) The woman's threat to kill her husband by poison so that she may take Joseph is a plot against this commandment from the start, and Joseph's answer in the Testament of Joseph is to refuse adultery. The commandment is the ground he stands on.
cards.member_note: Exodus 20:14 — *Thou shalt not commit adultery.* The commandment against adultery is what the woman asks Joseph to break and what he keeps.
